newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to keep ships at Sevastopol for 20 years.
newsitem.headline: Russia to keep ships at Sevastopol for 20 years.

text.p: The prime ministers of Russia and Ukraine signed a package of agreements on Wednesday giving Russia the right to base its part of the ex-Soviet Black Sea Fleet at Ukraine's naval base of Sevastopol for 20 years.

Ukraine's Pavlo Lazarenko and Russia's Viktor Chernomyrdin gave no financial details of the lease, which is aimed at solving one of the trickiest problems in relations between the neighbouring former Soviet republics.

Both premiers agreed that the deal, summarised in three documents, paved the way for Russian President Boris Yeltsin's visit to Kiev beginning on Friday and for the signing of a long-awaited friendship treaty on Saturday.
But Lazarenko made clear at a joint news conference that Ukraine was not ready to look beyond the 20-year term yet.
"The issue of prolonging the lease was not discussed today. Let's take time and see," Lazarenko said. "At least for the first 20 years," Chernomyrdin added.

The three documents signed by the premiers tackle the status of the Russian navy which will be based in Sevastopol on the Crimean peninsula, financial terms of the lease and criteria for the final shareout of the fleet.
But neither Chernomyrdin nor Lazarenko gave any indication of how much Russia would pay for the lease. "We will pay as much as is needed," Chernomyrdin said.
Russia and Ukraine have announced in the past they had reached a final deal on the fleet but many of their earlier commitments sank amid mutual mistrust and recrimination.

Chernomyrdin, who discussed the fleet's shareout with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma earlier on Wednesday, said the two countries had no outstanding problems in this area and that they would concentrate on carrying out Wednesday's decisions.
